messages:
maria: Heads-up — need clarity on event retention + key lifecycle for customer-facing audit logs before Friday's SOC review. Current docs are ambiguous about immutability vs retention windows.

dan: Agree. Quick Q: do we need true WORM (object lock) for all customers or only a subset (FedRAMP/Enterprise)? Also how do we show customers proof of immutability? :thinking_face:

ashley: For regulated customers we need WORM for 7 years. Most regular customers can have 1–3 year retention. We should support per-tenant retention policy + legal-hold override.

kevin: Implementation thought: envelope-encrypt events per-tenant with an archive key stored in an HSM-backed KMS. Active writes use rotating CMKs; archived blobs are re-encrypted with the archive key. That lets us rotate active keys while keeping archived objects decryptable.

maria: Is per-tenant CMK feasible in hosted? Cost and key quotas are a concern. Also need to decide if customer-facing events are plaintext or redacted (PII).

dan: Hosted can offer per-tenant CMKs as a premium feature (BYOK for Private customers already exists). For PII, redact fields and publish a hash for verification. Customers can verify audit integrity without seeing raw PII.

ashley: Schema proposal (high level): add event_version, retention_policy, legal_hold_id, kms_key_id, signature. Keep backward compatibility by mapping old fields to v1.

maria: Customer-facing validation idea: return a signed digest they can fetch and verify with our published public key. Example:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://console.redwood.com/archives/tenant123/event/abcd123
# response includes 'payload', 'signature', 'public_key_id'
echo "$payload" | openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature sig.bin
```

kevin: Ops question: prefer S3 Object Lock + Glacier Deep Archive for cost. Object Lock gives WORM semantics at object-level, but KMS must be set so Object Lock compliance remains valid — double-check provider docs. Also verify cross-region replication doesn't lose retention metadata.

dan: Backwards-compat note: add a 'schema_migration' endpoint to replay events into v2 format for customers that need it.

kevin: KMS specifics: use an archive key with restricted policy (decrypt allowed only for the archive service principal). Ensure key rotation doesn't break archived decrypts — store key version metadata in manifest. Consider multi-region keys and grants for emergency decrypts.

maria: Vuln triage / incident playbook items: if key compromise suspected: freeze writes, promote legal hold on affected tenants, copy archives to air-gapped HSM-backed storage, rotate keys, notify legal & SOC. We need a runbook.

ashley: I'll draft the runbook once schema + KMS gating are agreed. Can someone POC signing + verify and another person POC S3 Object Lock + CMK interaction in staging? I can own the runbook.

dan: I'll open a schema PR today. Quick snippet: {"event_version":"2","retention_policy":"tenant:7y","kms_key_id":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd","signature":"base64..."}

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll own KMS gating + staging POC for Object Lock + CMK. Will test decryptability across rotation.

maria: Also — make sure public-facing fetches replace internal actor IDs with stable external_id. Mapping only available via restricted API (NDA). We don't want accidental internal mapping leaks.

deploy-bot: New branch 'event-retention-mvp' opened by dan.

maria: Target: spec + runbook draft by Thu EOD, POC results in staging by next Tue. Thanks all.
